summary.intent: Run the GSD plan-phase workflow end-to-end for cipher-box phase 68.2 (SDK-owned read chain and resolved folder listings), then execute the resulting plans wave-by-wave, while also spinning up an isolated git worktree to start phase 69 in parallel.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.2 was fully planned (research, Nyquist VALIDATION.md, D-07 scope decision locked, pattern mapping, 12 plans/7 waves, plan-checker PASSED, coverage gates 13/13) and committed; execution proceeded sequentially through Waves 1-3 with independent spot-checks/re-runs passing, and a separate worktree was created at cipher-box-phase69 off origin/main for independent phase 69 work.

repo: gsd-tools query commit helper has a known false-negative: it reports `commit_failed` even when the commit lands cleanly in git log — always verify with `git log` before treating it as a real failure.

The `ui` capability plan:pre gate only fires when the hooks registry's `when` condition classifies a phase as a net-new UI surface; architecture/refactor phases like 68.2 correctly get zero UI hooks even though the lower-level ui-plan-gate check reports `block:true`.
Intel API-SURFACE extraction (§7.9) returned 0 symbols for this monorepo — it's HINT-only and safe to omit from planner input when empty rather than passing noise.
`worktree.baseRef: "head"` (not the `fresh`/origin-main default) means executor worktrees fork from live HEAD, so in-flight planning commits (e.g. new PLAN.md files) are visible to spawned executors.

This is a pnpm monorepo where worktree-based executors each need their own `pnpm install`, making per-wave worktree create/merge/cleanup expensive; sequential execution on the main tree reuses installed node_modules.
gap-analysis.plan-post check's JSON `rendered` field can contain control characters that break naive parsing — call the check directly instead of parsing the wrapped output.

code.finding: ROT-07 anti-rollback gate (RotationHighWater.enforceResolved) wired into root node resolve path (resolvePublishedNode).
ROT-07 gate also wired into dfsFindFolder's child-loop resolve, closing the read-path zero-gating gap identified in RESEARCH Pitfall 2.
Pre-existing write-path ROT-07 gate location, used as the reference pattern for the two new read-path gate sites.

resolveChildren's docstring documents that per-child resolve/unseal failures are skipped (graceful degradation) rather than swallowed at the folder level, because the target folder is already gated upstream via ensureFolderLoaded/dfsFindFolder — sibling omission is an availability tradeoff, not a security regression, since navigating into any child re-triggers the gate.

workflow: When an executor reports a deviation (e.g. widened error handling with changed test assertions) on security-adjacent code, read the actual implementation and re-run the security-relevant tests independently rather than trusting the self-reported SUMMARY.

For parallel independent phase work, `git worktree add` off a fetched/local origin/main ref keeps the new worktree free of the other phase's planning docs, while the original checkout keeps driving its own execution unaffected (shared .git, separate branches).
Prefer plain `git worktree add` over an EnterWorktree-style tool switch when the orchestrator needs to keep driving work in the current checkout rather than move into the new one.
When same-wave plans are file-disjoint but running in sequential (non-worktree) mode, serialize them in dependency-relevance order (critical-path plan first) to avoid git index contention.

Before AskUserQuestion-gated decisions with security or scope implications (e.g. D-07 grep-gate boundary), surface the concrete files/blast-radius affected by each option rather than an abstract choice.
